title: Redox and Electrochemistry - Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry - Oxidation and Reduction Concepts
subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: Which of the following statements best defines **oxidation** in terms of electron transfer?
questions.explain: According to the mnemonic **OIL RIG** (Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain), oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: In a redox reaction, the species that donates electrons is known as the:
questions.explain: The reducing agent loses electrons (is oxidized) and thereby causes the reduction of another species. Therefore, the electron donor is the reducing agent.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction:
$$Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) \rightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$$
Which species is acting as the **oxidizing agent**?
questions.explain: $Cu^{2+}$ gains electrons to become $Cu(s)$. Since it accepts electrons, it causes the oxidation of zinc, making $Cu^{2+}$ the oxidizing agent.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: In the reaction $2Na(s) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2NaCl(s)$, which element is oxidized?
questions.explain: Sodium ($Na$) starts with an oxidation number of 0 and ends with +1 in $NaCl$. An increase in oxidation number indicates oxidation.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: Which of the following processes represents a **reduction**?
questions.explain: Reduction is the gain of electrons. In option b, the chlorine molecule gains two electrons to form chloride ions ($Cl^-$).
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry
